summary: Model family choice has a large and statistically significant effect on predictive performance on the Adult Income dataset. Gradient Boosting achieves 0.9193 ROC-AUC while Decision Trees achieve only 0.7480, a 22.9% relative improvement. This difference was highly statistically significant (p < 0.000001) and stable across 25 cross-validation folds.
primary_metric_name: ROC-AUC difference between best and worst model families
direction: Gradient Boosting >> Decision Tree (ensemble methods dominate; tree-based dominates linear methods)
methodological_choices: Binary classification (<=50K vs >50K). Preprocessing: removed 3616 rows with missing values in workclass, occupation, or native-country (93% of data retained). Categorical features label-encoded; numeric features standardized. Evaluated 7 model families: Logistic Regression, Decision Tree, Random Forest (100 trees), Gradient Boosting (100 trees), SVM (RBF kernel), KNN (k=5), Gaussian Naive Bayes. Primary metric: ROC-AUC (robust to class imbalance: 76% negative, 24% positive). Evaluation: 5-fold stratified cross-validation repeated 5 times with different random seeds (25 total folds) using stratified splits to preserve class balance.
verification_method: 5x5 Repeated Stratified K-Fold Cross-Validation (25 total folds). Examined per-fold stability: all models showed tight distributions (ranges 0.01-0.02 ROC-AUC). Paired t-test on fold-level scores confirmed ranking. Effect size analysis (Cohen's d = 42.25) confirmed practical significance.
verification_result: Finding CONFIRMED and STRENGTHENED. The massive effect size (Cohen's d=42.25, t=148.1, p<0.000001) demonstrates this is not a random artifact. Random Forest (0.9054) and Gradient Boosting (0.9193) consistently outperform linear models (0.8508 LogReg, 0.8484 KNN) and Decision Trees (0.7480). Across all 25 folds, Gradient Boosting was never lower than Random Forest, confirming robust ordering. Model family is the dominant factor in this dataset's performance—far more important than typical hyperparameter tuning.
